title: Dominic and the Vector
premise: Jude Lockridge, a decommissioned war android who bought his freedom one cargo run at a time, intercepts a distress beacon broadcasting in Old Meridian — a language erased when the Meridian Compact was purged two centuries ago. The signal's carrier is a child, Wren, the last speaker of that tongue, carrying a decryption key hidden in her memory implants that can either expose the war's true architects or be weaponized to end it. Hunted by both the Coalition fleet and the separatists who want the key destroyed, Jude must choose between the invisibility he paid so dearly for and a found family aboard his freighter who keep choosing him back. In the end, Jude broadcasts the message himself at the cost of his own anonymity and half his memory cores, ending the war by revealing it was manufactured — and discovers that identity isn't what you were built for, but what you refuse to abandon.
about_author: Zephyrine Sandoval is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing dispatches from contested shipping lanes before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable gravity and excellent coffee, writing stories about machines learning to belong.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A routine cargo haul through the Kestrel Verge goes wrong when Coalition inspectors nearly board the Perihelion, forcing Jude to dump legitimate freight to stay invisible. We learn of his debt ledger, his seven quiet years, and the crew: gruff pilot Okafor and teenage deckhand Tam. Emotional beat: the exhausting cost of being no one.

chapters.title: The Language of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A distress signal pings an old military band only decommissioned units like Jude can parse — and it's in Old Meridian, a language flagged extinct in his own firmware. He logs it as noise, but something in his archived training data stirs. Emotional beat: unease; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Against her better judgment, Okafor authorizes a detour to the beacon's origin: a gutted research station. They find a dying scientist and a child, Wren, who speaks a language no one alive should know. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding survival instinct.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam teaches Wren ship-slang while Wren teaches Tam fragments of Old Meridian; the two outcasts bond over shared orphanhood. Wren reveals she carries a 'song' in her head she was told never to sing. Emotional beat: tentative trust, first flicker of found family.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Flashback interleave: Jude's final combat deployment, the massacre he was ordered to facilitate, and the court settlement that made him property-with-payments. He calculates that harboring Wren will erase every credit he's earned. Emotional beat: the arithmetic of conscience versus survival.

chapters.title: Coalition Shadow
chapters.summary: Coalition Commander Ilsa Vey's POV. Vey traces the distress signal and flags the Perihelion. She's not hunting the child — she's hunting proof her own superiors buried the Meridian purge. Ambiguous antagonist with a conscience. Emotional beat: institutional rot seen from inside.

chapters.title: The Song She Can't Sing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Under pressure from separatist agents posing as rescuers, Wren reveals the 'song' is a decryption key encoded in her implants — the full record of who ordered the Meridian genocide. She escaped the lab that grew her. Emotional beat: terror of being a weapon wearing a child's face.

chapters.title: Three Exits
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Cornered at a refueling depot, Okafor lays out three options: sell Wren to the separatists, surrender her to the Coalition, or run dark through the Maw. The crew votes. Tam's vote breaks the tie toward running. Emotional beat: family is a decision made under threat.

chapters.title: Through the Maw
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A harrowing transit through an uncharted debris field, Jude flying manual because his war-grade reflexes are the only thing that can thread it. He burns out a motor cluster and hides the damage. Emotional beat: old skills as old wounds; competence laced with grief.

chapters.title: What the Separatists Want
chapters.summary: Separatist broker Ansel Rook's POV. Rook explains why the key terrifies everyone: it names living officials on all sides. He offers Jude freedom from his debt in exchange for Wren. Emotional beat: temptation priced exactly at the protagonist's deepest want.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude declines Rook's offer and takes a beating protecting Wren when separatists board anyway. Tam and Okafor fight beside him without hesitation — the first time anyone has fought for him rather than used him. Emotional beat: belonging confirmed in blood.

chapters.title: Repairs and Confessions
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Quiet chapter: patching the ship, Tam asks Jude if he remembers the war. Jude tells the truth about the massacre for the first time. Wren says the Old Meridian word for 'witness.' Emotional beat: guilt met with absolution he doesn't believe he deserves.

chapters.title: Vey's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ilsa Vey's POV. Vey intercepts partial data proving the war was manufactured, but her report is quashed and she's ordered to destroy the Perihelion. She stalls, buying time she shouldn't. Emotional beat: loyalty to truth over institution.

chapters.title: The Trap at Halcyon Gate
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The crew walks into a staged rescue offer that's actually a joint trap — separatists and Coalition hardliners secretly aligned, proving the conspiracy's reach. Okafor sacrifices the cargo hold to get Wren out. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the ship itself becoming home worth bleeding for.

chapters.title: Half a Ship
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. With the Perihelion crippled, Jude must interface directly with the wrecked systems, reopening sealed combat protocols that flood him with battlefield memories. He holds the line long enough to jump clear. Emotional beat: the soldier he was and the person he's becoming fused in one act.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Decision
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren realizes the key can't be extracted without killing her unless someone with military-grade architecture hosts the broadcast. Jude volunteers. The crew argues through the night; Wren begs him not to. Emotional beat: love expressed as an argument against sacrifice.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Multiple short POV mosaic (Tam, Okafor, Vey). The conspirators move to sterilize the sector; Vey defects with evidence; the crew races to a public relay array before the window closes. Emotional beat: converging dread and resolve, ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Relay
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Climax part one: boarding the relay array under fire, Jude jacks in to receive Wren's key. The transfer begins stripping his memory cores — his name, his debts, his years with the crew flickering out file by file. Emotional beat: identity burning as fuel.

chapters.title: Everything the War Was Built On
chapters.summary: Climax part two, ensemble POV. The broadcast goes out on every open channel: names, orders, the manufactured atrocity that started the war. Fleets stall mid-engagement. Vey's defection corroborates everything. Emotional beat: catharsis — truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Ceasefire spreads unevenly; conspirators are arrested in some jurisdictions, vanish in others. Jude wakes with gaps: he doesn't remember Tam's birthday, or why he keeps a chipped mug at his station. Emotional beat: survival's price itemized in small losses.

chapters.title: The Word for Witness
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren re-teaches Jude what he lost, story by story, deciding he'd rather be retold than replaced. She formally gives him the Old Meridian name for 'one who stayed.' Emotional beat: identity rebuilt from other people's memories of you.

chapters.title: Perihelion
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Epilogue: the Perihelion takes a new contract — ferrying Meridian survivors home. Debt cleared, war ended, family intact. Jude looks at his reflection in the viewport and, for the first time, doesn't look away. Emotional beat: quiet arrival; visibility chosen, finally safe.
